severity: CRITICAL — would have silently broken the live Streamlit demo
bug: normalize_scores() computed min/max from the INPUT ARRAY ITSELF. For batch evaluation (1398 rows) this is fine. For single-transaction scoring (any live/manual check), min==max for a 1-element array by definition, forcing normalized score to ALWAYS be 0.0 regardless of the actual raw score. Every live transaction check would have shown the same near-minimum risk score no matter what was entered.
how_found: 3 adversarial stress-test scenarios (tiny burst payments, device spoofing, Rs.25000 spike) all returned the IDENTICAL score 0.0024 — an impossible coincidence that revealed the bug.
fix: Compute fixed normalization bounds (min, 99.5th percentile) once from the TRAINING distribution, persist to normalization_bounds.json, and require them for any single-transaction or small-batch scoring. Batch bounds only used when explicitly omitted (full-set evaluation).
action_required: app/streamlit_app.py's score_transaction() function MUST be updated to load normalization_bounds.json and pass bounds= into ensemble_score() — otherwise the live demo has this exact bug.
